subject: Social Media
title: The Illusory Truth Effect
description: A quick, practical guide to The Illusory Truth Effect.

hook.text: Hear a claim once and you're skeptical. Hear it ten times and it feels true. Repetition replaces evidence.

buildup.text: Psychologists Hasher, Goldstein, and Toppino proved this in 1977. Repeated statements feel more familiar, thus truer.

discovery.text: Social media supercharges repetition. A false claim seen across multiple accounts feels like consensus.

twist.text: Even knowing a claim is false doesn't eliminate the effect. Familiarity still makes it feel more credible.

climax.text: This is why corrections on platforms fail—the false claim was seen 50 times; the correction, once.

punchline.text: Repetition doesn't make things true. It makes them feel true.

quiz.question: What does the illusory truth effect exploit?
